events.summary: STORY: Unionized workers at South Korea's Kakao staged a four-hour strike and rally on Wednesday.They demanded job security and changes to the tech firm's bonus system. Hundreds of workers wearing black T-shirts and holding white umbrellas walked out of Kakao's office in the morning.The union had told police as many as 1,200 members would join the rally.Local media reported the union plans a general strike for June 29 with all 5,000 members due to take part.Kakao operates South Korea's biggest messaging app by users, and employs about 6,000 people.The dispute comes with growing labor unrest in South Korea as tech firms score record earnings during the global AI boom.Samsung Electronics' union got ⁠a ​deal this month tying chip division bonuses to ​10.5% of operating profit.Kakao said last month it had failed to reach a wage deal with the union in government-mediated talks.The union wants reform to Kakao's compensation system.They argue executives have received higher bonus payments in recent years while other employees have seen limited benefits.Kakao previously said it turned down a union demand for profit-sharing, calling it unrealistic.The union refused to confirm details on the negotiation.Kakao said Wednesday its running a real-time system in response to the strike.It added management will keep talking with the union.

events.summary: South Korea's Kakao Corp union said on Monday it will stage a four-hour strike ‌and rally in Pangyo on June 10, demanding job ‌security and reforms to a compensation system it says disproportionately rewards executives.  In a ​statement, the union said its core demands include halting restructuring such as divestments and spin-offs and improving what it called an "executive-centric pay system" that fuels job insecurity.  The move ⁠comes after government-mediated wage talks broke down last week, with Kakao rejecting union demands — including profit-sharing proposals — as unrealistic and "a big ​burden" on ​management as it prioritises investment ​and shareholder returns.
events.title: Union at South Korea's Kakao to hold partial strike on June 10

events.summary: Kadant Inc. (NYSE:KAI) shares dropped 1% in after-hours trading following the announcement of its CEO succession plan. Michael Colwell will become president and COO on October 1, 2026, and then president, CEO, and director on January 2, 2027, succeeding current CEO Jeffrey Powell, who will transition to executive chairman. The plan aims to ensure leadership continuity, with Powell remaining involved in strategic activities.
events.title: Kadant stock slips on CEO succession plan announcement By Investing.com

events.summary: Tesla's stock fell by approximately 0.6% to $365.46 as China's massive vehicle production surplus intensified pressure on the company. China's capacity to build almost twice as many vehicles as its domestic market can absorb is leading to an influx of excess supply into global markets, threatening Tesla's pricing power. This competitive environment is particularly impactful for Tesla, as its automotive gross margin was 16.3% in the second quarter, while capital expenditures were $5.8 billion and free cash flow was negative by about $1.1 billion.
events.title: Tesla Slips as China Turns Factory Surplus Into a Global Threat

events.summary: General Motors is increasingly relying on its truck and traditional combustion vehicle sales as demand for electric vehicles cools, particularly after federal incentive changes. While showcasing its expanded Cadillac electric lineup on World EV Day, GM noted a sequential decline in EV unit volume. The company continues to fund its electrification efforts using profits from its robust truck segment, adapting its strategy to a challenging EV market while maintaining its long-term commitment to electric vehicles.
events.title: General Motors (NYSE:GM) Leans on Trucks As Electric Vehicle Demand Cools

events.summary: Intel's stock fell 4% after Piper Sandler initiated coverage with a Neutral rating and a $110 price target, citing limited near-term upside despite the company's manufacturing progress. The brokerage acknowledged Intel's efforts to improve technology and expand its foundry business but highlighted execution challenges and intense competition in the semiconductor market as concerns. These factors are expected to temper further gains for the chipmaker.
events.title: Intel Stock Plunges 4% as Piper Sandler Turns Neutral on Chipmaker

events.summary: Plug Power Inc. is experiencing decreased demand in several core product categories, leading to a 17.4% year-over-year decline in equipment and infrastructure revenues in Q2 2026. The article also compares Plug Power's performance to peers like Bloom Energy and Flux Power, noting PLUG's stock performance and valuation metrics.
events.title: Is Sluggish Equipment Demand a Concern for Plug Power Stock?

events.summary: Middleby (MIDD) shares have dropped 10.9% since its last earnings report, underperforming the S&P 500. events.summary: Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE:FCX) shares dropped over 5% in premarket trading on Thursday as copper prices pulled back from a record high achieved earlier in the session. The increase in copper prices has been attributed to concerns about tightening inventories outside the U.S. and metal moving into U.S. warehouses ahead of potential tariffs.
events.title: Freeport-McMoRan Shares Fall More Than 5% as Copper Retreats From Record High

events.summary: Packaging Corporation of America (PCA) anticipates meeting or exceeding its third-quarter earnings guidance due to strong operations, firm pricing, and a tight containerboard market, despite agricultural weakness impacting corrugated volume.
